ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 23 of 27 April 2015 (Ley 23 de 2015, unified AML/CFT framework, as amended), Law 41 of 1 October 2000, and related UAF resolutions; UBO register governed by Law 254 of 28 October 2022 and Executive Decree 180 of 2023, administered by the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministry of Economy and Finance, with supervisory oversight by the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) and the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, UBOs, and beneficial controllers against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, UK consolidated list, and the Panamanian UAF PEP database; Politically Exposed Persons as defined under Law 23 of 2015, including family members and close associates, require enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth review, and senior management approval prior to incorporation and ongoing monitoring.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá – Online Name Search and Certification System (Certificado de Búsqueda / Vista de Nombre), https://www.registro-publico.gob.pa
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be available in the registry index and may be presented in any language using the Latin alphabet; the name must include the expression 'Sociedad Anónima' or the abbreviation 'S.A.', must be transliterated into standard Latin script where applicable, and must not be identical or confusingly similar to names already registered or reserved in the Registro Público de Panamá.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of the proposed name, the applicant, acting through a licensed Panamanian attorney, may file a written 'recurso de reconsideración' with the Director General del Registro Público de Panamá within five (5) business days of notification, followed, if necessary, by a 'recurso de apelación' before the same authority; the appeal must demonstrate that the name is not confusingly similar to existing registrations and must include the statutory appeal fee; the 30-day reservation window cannot be extended and a new search certificate is required upon its expiration.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A physical registered office in Panama is statutorily mandatory and must be provided through a licensed resident agent; remote and virtual operations of the maternity and infant care e-commerce business are permissible without local physical premises, provided the entity substantiates economic substance through contracts, payment-rail records (Stripe, PayPal), and territorial-source tax filings; a virtual office service cannot replace the incumbent resident agent requirement.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: estimated 5–10% probability of unannounced physical on-site inspection within the first 24 months for a standard-risk, non-licensed e-commerce corporation; the DGI, UAF, and Superintendencia de Bancos retain unrestricted inspection powers over the registered agent's premises, books, and records.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Panama General Corporation Law — Ley No. 32 of 26 February 1927, as amended (especially Articles 1–14 on constitution of the Sociedad Anónima); complementary provisions in Código Judicial, Book I, Title IX (Registry of Persons); and Ley No. 23 of 2017 imposing anti-money-laundering obligations on Resident Agents and corporate shareholders.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Dirección de Registro de Personas Jurídicas / Mercantil Section
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución (public deed of incorporation protocolized before a Notary of the Circuit) together with the Formulario de Inscripción de Personas Jurídicas
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum fully paid-up capital under Law 32 of 1927; standard formation provides authorized capital of USD 10,000 represented by 100 registered or bearer shares of USD 100 par value, with at least one share subscribed; no escrow or bank-deposit precondition at incorporation — fully paid-up capital documentation is instead demanded during bank and payment-rail KYC/onboarding procedures.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF SOCIEDAD ANÓNIMA. The undersigned Sole Director of the Company hereby resolves: (1) the subscription and issuance of 100 ordinary shares, par value USD 100 each, to the subscriber named in the share ledger, is approved; (2) the registered office is fixed at the address stated in the public deed and the Resident Agent is ratified; (3) the officers President, Secretary, and Treasurer are appointed with full statutory powers; (4) opening the Company's bank and payment-rail accounts is authorized; and (5) incorporation and pre-operating expenses are ratified. Unanimously passed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Availability Search and Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Quiosco de Consulta de Personas Jurídicas / Mercantil Section front desk
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit three alternative proposed corporate names via the Public Registry's online name-consultation portal or in person at the Mercantil Section. The registry compares each candidate against live corporate records for exact or phonetically identical matches. Upon clearance, obtain the constancia de nombre (name availability certificate), which is valid for 30 days and must be attached to the draft public deed.
required_dossiers: Three proposed corporate names in descending priority
Notarized power of attorney (Poder) of the incorporating attorney-in-fact
Identification document of the applicant legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for phonetic similarity or reserved use, file a reconsideration request or immediately submit the next alternative name; rejected filings attract no penalty within the reservation window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of the Public Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública del Circuito de Panamá (Circuit Notary)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The shareholders execute a Poder authorizing a resident Panamanian attorney to subscribe the incorporation deed. The attorney drafts the Escritura Pública de Constitución containing the company name, domicile, duration, authorized capital, classes of shares, corporate governance form (Sole Director, S.A.), the Resident Agent designation and registered office address. The deed is read, ratified, and signed by the attorney-in-fact on behalf of subscribers before the Notary, then protocolized into the notarial register.
required_dossiers: Notarized Poder General or Poder Especial of the subscribing attorney
Draft by-laws (Estatutos) with governance provisions
Passport copies of subscribers and initial directors
Name availability certificate issued in Step 1
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Notary identifies statutory omissions, such as missing share classes or absence of the Resident Agent clause, the deed is immediately re-drafted and re-signed; re-protocolization preserves the intended incorporation date with no registry prejudice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of the Corporation at the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Dirección de Registro de Personas Jurídicas
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the certified notarial testimonio of the Escritura Pública together with the Formulario de Inscripción de Personas Jurídicas and proof of payment of the official registration fee. The Registry assigns the Ficha corporate identification number and issues the Inscripción certificate. Legal personality is effective upon this registration; expedited processing is available upon payment of the urgency supplement.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the notarial public deed of incorporation
Completed Formulario de Inscripción de Personas Jurídicas
Official fee payment receipt
Resident Agent acceptance letter, when required by registry policy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a prevención (defect notice), the attorney-in-fact must cure the omission and re-file within 10 working days; on expiry the file is archived, and a fresh filing with a corrective brief may be submitted without loss of corporate name priority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration (RUC) and Social Security Employer Enrollment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas — Sede Electrónica; Caja de Seguro Social (CSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the Registro Único de Contribuyente (RUC) through the DGI online tax portal, attaching the registered Escritura and identification of the legal representative. Obtain the RUC certificate and the DGI 'Aviso de Operación' tax filing. Separately register as an employer (patrono) with the CSS if personnel will be hired at any stage.
required_dossiers: Inscripción issued by the Public Registry
Valid passport or cedula of the legal representative
Proof of registered office address
Contact details of the tax accounting representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where DGI identifies inconsistency between the deed and RUC application, the application is electronically corrected and resubmitted; a preventive clarification meeting with the DGI fiscalization officer may be requested to avoid future audit triggers.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Commercial Operating Notice and License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipio de Panamá — Tesorería Municipal and the corresponding Junta Comunal window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Aviso de Operación through the municipal online licensing module or at the local Junta Comunal office, declaring the e-commerce retail activity under ISIC 4791 (online sales of maternity and infant commodities). Pay the proportional annual municipal operating fee (patente municipal / tasa de operación) and obtain the Permiso de Operación, which must be renewed annually.
required_dossiers: RUC certificate and DGI Aviso de Operación
Registered office address proof
Identification of the legal representative
Certified copy of the Public Registry inscription
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality disputes the activity code or the declared address, submit a corrected sworn statement referring to the DGI activity classification; late-correction fines are avoided by prompt payment of the adjusted municipal fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Books, Resident Agent Compliance, and Banking/Payment-Rail Readiness
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Resident Agent (licensed Panamanian attorney); Registro Público de Panamá (optional book deposition); DGI for annual franchise tax
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the corporate minute book and share subscription ledger, and where applicable register them under the Public Registry's libro digital deposition procedure. Ensure the Resident Agent named in the deed is active. Prepare the AML/KYC file for bank and payment-rail onboarding, including beneficial ownership declaration, and note the obligation to pay the annual franchise tax (currently USD 300 for the S.A.) to DGI one year after incorporation.
required_dossiers: Corporate minute book and share subscription ledger
Beneficial ownership declaration and KYC forms
RUC certificate and municipality license
Payment-rail onboarding forms for Stripe and PayPal
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late franchise tax triggers a 10% surcharge and possible temporary suspension from the registry; immediate payment with interest through the DGI portal restores standing without criminal liability for a first default.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — the enterprise is a pure e-commerce retail operator under ISIC 4791 with no manufacturing or fabrication plant. If the company later adds local warehousing, light packaging, or product transformation, the Dirección General de Normas y Tecnología Industrial of the Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) would become the competent industrial authority.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación / Permiso de Operación Municipal issued by the Municipality of Panama, complemented by the DGI tax Aviso de Operación; no separate national industrial operating license is required for online resale of maternity and infant commodities.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) — Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category I (bajo impacto) — exemption from a full EIA Report; only the simplified Registro de Operación / Category I declaration form and payment of the administrative fee are required for the e-commerce distribution center and small warehouse footprint.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process effluents or industrial emissions generated. For ancillary warehousing and logistics: comply with municipal sewer and wastewater standards under Ley 44 de 2002; waste handling per Ley 1 de 2008 and DIGESA regulations; single-use plastic restrictions in packaging per Ley 95 de 2020; VOC thresholds not applicable absent printing, chemical, or manufacturing operations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For the e-commerce office and warehouse premises: obtain the Visto Bueno (fire safety inspection certificate) from the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá; complete the municipal structural and occupancy inspection for the leased facility; and if personnel are hired, register with the Caja de Seguro Social and post the workplace health and safety notice (Reglamento Interno de Higiene y Seguridad) required by MITRADEL.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF); official portal: Sede Electrónica de la DGI / 'T@x Panamá' (https://www.dgi.gob.pa)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident owner forms a Panama Sociedad Anónima (S.A.) through a licensed registered agent, files incorporation articles with the Public Registry, obtains a legal domicile, then applies to the DGI for a RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente). The application must include corporate excerpts, bylaws, registered agent certification, appointment of directors/officers, and proof of local address. The RUC is granted electronically or at DGI service offices and the entity is simultaneously registered for ITBMS, withholding tax, and other tax obligations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election exists. All Panamanian S.A. corporations are automatically taxed as separate entity-level taxpayers. Eligible businesses may elect special incentive regimes: Multinational Headquarters (SEM) under Law 41 of 2007, Panama-Pacífico Special Economic Zone, or City of Knowledge, subject to qualifying activities. Small taxpayers with annual gross turnover not exceeding B/.20,000 may elect the simplified small-taxpayer ITBMS regime.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general minimum sales threshold for ITBMS registration; habitual commercial sellers must register regardless of volume. A simplified small-taxpayer regime is available for annual gross turnover up to B/.20,000, above which standard 7% ITBMS is charged on taxable transfers and services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama mandates electronic invoicing for registered taxpayers through the DGI's 'T@x' system. Invoice data must be transmitted in DGI-validated XML format using a digital signature certificate; a QR-code/electronic stamp and DGI transaction authorization code must be included before the sale is considered fiscally complete. Clearance and authorization occur in near real time via the DGI API gateway.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods qualify for 0% ITBMS where they are physically exported from Panamanian territory to a foreign destination under a valid customs export declaration. Services are zero-rated when rendered from Panama to a non-resident recipient with the benefit and use occurring wholly outside Panama, or when provided as part of an export transaction. The exporter must be an active registered ITBMS taxpayer and maintain contemporaneous proof of export and foreign receipt.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or Air Waybill proving physical departure from Panama
Commercial Invoice listing the foreign buyer and shipment terms
Inward remittance evidence (bank SWIFT/MT103 or payment gateway settlement report showing foreign funds received in Panama or on behalf of the exporting entity)
Packaging list and contract of sale showing title transfer to a foreign customer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI may audit export dossiers and disprove zero-rating where export entries, transport documents, or payment repatriation are missing or inconsistent. False claims are treated as ITBMS evasion: the 0% rate is reversed, and the taxpayer must pay the full 7% ITBMS on gross proceeds, plus monthly late-payment interest of 1% per month, a penalty ranging from 100% to 300% of the omitted tax, and potential criminal liability of two to six years' imprisonment under Panama's tax criminal provisions (Law 70 of 2019).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Republic of Panama has no central bank with monetary, monetary-exchange, or capital-control functions. The banking supervisory authority is the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (Superintendency of Banks of Panama, 'SBP'), established under Decreto Ley No. 2 of 2008 as amended. The Panamanian fiscal agent is Banco Nacional de Panamá, a state-owned commercial bank, which does not perform central-bank FX regulation. The Unidad de Análisis Financiero ('UAF') and the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas jointly enforce AML/CFT obligations, including the beneficial-ownership reporting regime under Law 70 of 2019.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Panamanian Balboa (PAB) is a nominal accounting unit pegged at 1:1 to the US dollar; no Balboa banknotes are issued, and the USD is legal tender for all domestic and cross-border obligations. Panama maintains a fully liberalised capital and current account regime: there are no surrender, conversion, licensing, prior-approval, or repatriation restrictions on any currency. Non-resident shareholders may freely remit dividends, loan repayments, branch profits, and liquidation proceeds. The only relevant frictions are fiscal: profits sourced outside Panama fall outside the territorial tax net, while dividends distributed out of Panamanian-source taxable profits attract a 10% withholding dividend tax (or 5% for registered shares); the municipal, educational, and shareholder-accounting formalities apply solely to Panama-source income. No exchange-control approval is required for an e-commerce operation collecting USD revenue from online buyers and settling to a Panama S.A. bank account.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Panama imposes no statutory deadline for export proceeds repatriation, no mandatory conversion ratio, no requirement to channel export receipts through a designated central-bank account, and no withholding on export proceeds. For AML documentary integrity, banks request the commercial invoice, packing list, Bill of Lading/Air Waybill, and the Panama customs declaration to evidence the underlying cross-border sale. For digital maternity and baby supplies sales, an equivalent evidentiary bundle comprises the merchant agreement, platform settlement statements, and order-level invoices.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational account with merchant acquiring integration
Operational account with fintech-friendly digital onboarding

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banco Nacional de Panamá (state-owned fiscal agent bank)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM-HIGH as a payment-acquirer collection channel (Stripe, PayPal, Shopify Payments) and LOW as a standalone domestic clearing rail. Panama has no dedicated e-money licence; digital banking and fintech pilot programmes operate through the SBP regulatory sandbox and can enable limited electronic-money issuance under a full banking licence. An offshore EMI or non-bank PSP without a Panama banking licence cannot access the Panamanian ACH or the domestic clearing system, and Panamanian Tier-1 banks generally treat incoming credits from an unlicensed foreign EMI as higher-risk third-party payments. The recommended treasury architecture is a Panama S.A. USD account at a Tier-1 licensed bank receiving daily settlement payout wires from Stripe/PayPal through their US correspondent banks; the offshore EMI should be used only for regional payout collection, with periodic SWIFT sweeps into the Panama account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A Panama S.A. must maintain a resident agent and, practically, a Panamanian legal representative; however, banks uniformly require at least one director or the authorised corporate officer to attend an in-person onboarding interview at a Panama branch or at a recognised regional affiliate (e.g., Miami or Central American offices) before account activation. Remote opening is available only on a discretionary basis for low-risk clients using apostilled corporate documents, notarised signature verification by a Panamanian attorney, a sworn beneficial-owner declaration, an economic-substance statement, and a live video-KYC session. Fully paperless onboarding is not the norm; the majority of Tier-1 banks mandate biometric identity verification during the interview; state-owned and conservative banks may additionally require a second director or local director attendance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Panama S.A. with bearer shares, nominal shareholders, or a beneficial-owner chain not matched in the national Registro de Beneficiarios Finales (RBF, Law 70/2019)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Filed RBF registry excerpt showing the full natural-person UBO chain; certified share register and share transfer ledger; certified copy of the board resolution appointing officers; Panamanian counsel AML opinion; sworn affidavit of source of funds for each shareholder; copy of the registered agent agreement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High intra-month payment velocity from cross-border e-commerce aggregators (Stripe, PayPal) without an invoice-level or shipment-level trail
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed merchant agreements with Stripe/PayPal; 12-month platform settlement reports; ERP sales ledger with line-item invoices; courier and last-mile delivery records; returns and refund policy documentation; historical 90-day bank statements from the current payment processor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors or ultimate beneficial owners domiciled in high-risk, sanctioned, or tax-blacklist jurisdictions, or classification as politically exposed persons (PEPs)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Individual PEP and adverse-media declaration; passport and residency proof; professional reference letter from a reputable correspondent bank or internationally recognised counsel; certified criminal-record certificate; written commercial rationale for the Panama structure and proof that the e-commerce operations, inventory, and customers are located outside the high-risk jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large initial capital injection into a newly opened dormant account before e-commerce turnover is verifiable
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank reference letter from the remitting bank; board resolution authorising the capital call; share subscription agreement; pro-forma or audited financial statements; tax residency certificate of the shareholder; customer and supplier contracts demonstrating operational readiness of the maternity and baby supplies online business.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Step 1 - Adopt a board resolution authorising the issuance of registered shares at an agreed subscription price and update the Panama Share Registry. Step 2 - Execute an international SWIFT MT103 wire from the shareholder's account to the Panama S.A. account, entering in Field 70 the ISO 20022 purpose code 'INVS' or 'EQUI' with the narrative 'Paid-in capital subscription' plus the company name and RUC. Step 3 - Deliver to the receiving bank the apostilled Certificado de Registro (Articles of Incorporation), the certified directors' resolution, the share subscription agreement, the economic-substance statement, and the RUC taxpayer card. Step 4 - No SBP approval, registration, or FX declaration is required; the bank will only screen the transaction under its AML thresholds. For operating capital, receivables from Stripe/PayPal must be presented as trade proceeds supported by merchant agreements and platform settlement reports, otherwise the bank may reclassify them as unexplained third-party payments and freeze the funds pending further KYC.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Domestic USD disbursements inside Panama settle through the Panamanian ACH and the Cámara de Compensación operated by Banco Nacional de Panamá, suitable for payroll, rent, and local supplier payments. International trade disbursements use: (i) SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers for direct wire payments to overseas suppliers; (ii) SWIFT MT202/MT202 COV for correspondent interbank transfers; and (iii) commercial letters of credit (SWIFT MT700) for large inventory purchases, negotiated in USD under UCP600, with reimbursements effected via MT740/MT756 or MT202 COV. Standby letters of credit (SWIFT MT760) may support B2B material procurement commitments. Stripe and PayPal payout cycles terminate as USD credits to the Panama account through the processor's US clearing integration (ACH or wire), requiring no PAB conversion or central-bank reporting.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards between USD and EUR, GBP, or CNH executed with an SBP-regulated Tier-1 bank or its US/European broker affiliate, used to hedge supplier invoices denominated in non-USD currencies.
European-style FX options and collar structures on non-USD settlement currencies for inventory procurement in the maternity and baby supplies supply chain.
Cross-currency basis swaps matching USD working capital against the operating currency of the principal sourcing market.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not applicable between PAB and USD because Panama has no independent Balboa money market; the USD is the domestic legal tender, so FX hedging necessarily references only externally traded currencies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Impuesto Único de Personas Jurídicas (Annual Franchise Tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due annually on or before 31 March of each calendar year; payment made exclusively through the DGI online payment platform or commercial bank agent network.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly late-payment surcharge of 5% applied from day after deadline (capped at 50% by the Panamanian Tax Code); failure for three consecutive years may lead to administrative strike-off by the Registro Público and cancellation of the resident agent services.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Declaración Jurada de Beneficiario Final (Final Beneficial Owner Annual Declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (Registry under Law 23 of 2015, as amended by Law 70 of 2019)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due annually on or before 31 October of each calendar year; newly incorporated entities must submit an initial declaration within 30 days from registration.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monetary fine of USD 1,000 per violation, potential restriction on share transfers, and inability to obtain certification of good standing until the declaration is filed; may also be considered a criminal offence under anti-money laundering provisions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited Financial Statements and Independent Auditor’s Report (only when statutory thresholds are exceeded)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due with the annual income tax return, generally by 31 March of the fiscal year immediately following the close of the tax period; extension requests are subject to DGI prior grant.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Tax Code penalties for failure to present audited statements, including fines up to USD 5,000 for negligence and tax assessment adjustments; continuous non-compliance may support revocation of operating permits or public registry restrictions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit required under Panamanian tax law if the corporation has gross annual income exceeding USD 3,000,000 or total net assets exceeding USD 5,000,000; audit requirement also applies to licensed financial, fiduciary, and public-interest entities regardless of size.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted by the College of Public Accountants of Panama; local GAAP is acceptable only for non-publicly traded and non-licensed entities below the statutory audit threshold.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each Sociedad Anónima must file an annual beneficial owner declaration confirming the current chain of ownership, including intermediate holding entities and ultimate natural persons holding 10% or more shares, voting control, or significant management influence. The confirmation must be uploaded to the Registro Público’s electronic platform; changes in shareholding during the year must be reported in the next annual confirmation and the register of members must be updated with transfer details and dates.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday or preferential rate applies to online retail of maternity/infant supplies. Standard 25% corporate income tax applies to Panama-source net income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 1 (Personas Jurídicas) – Annual Corporate Income Tax Return filed through the DGI e-Tax portal (Sistema de Tareas Digitales / www.dgi.gob.pa).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly advance tax payments (Formulario 1-Q or e-Tax payment slips) are due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, and 15 December for calendar-year taxpayers.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return must be filed within three months after the fiscal year-end (by 31 March for a calendar-year company); if the final balance is due, payment must accompany the return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer Identification Number (RUC) of the Sociedad Anónima, as registered in the Public Registry and DGI.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The local resident agent or authorized representative must insert the company RUC; non-resident shareholders are not identified individually on the return.
Use the statutory fiscal year approved by the shareholders; a change in fiscal year requires DGI authorization.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All Panama-source gross income, including online sales of maternity and infant commodities, net of returns, discounts, and refunds.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude foreign-source receipts; include only sales delivered into Panama or generating income from Panamanian customers; e-commerce payment processor settlements must be reconciled.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowable deductions related to gross income: inventory cost, shipping/logistics, payment processor fees, marketing, salaries, hosting, and depreciation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions must be documented with invoices from suppliers; cross-border service payments must be supported by withholding tax certificates; otherwise the deduction is disallowed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income minus operating deductions; computed strictly under Panama territorial tax rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-source income and exempt Panama-source income (if any) are excluded; all Panama-source activity must be fully reported.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Available loss carryforward from prior periods, limited to 5 tax years.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss records and audited amounts should be retained; NOL claims must conform to prior filed returns.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after applying the NOL carryforward cap.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders cannot offset losses; the entity's tax base is independent of profit distribution decisions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base multiplied by the 25% statutory rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The company is the taxpayer; no foreign tax credit may be claimed on this return for Panama-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credit for the four quarterly advance payments (pagos a cuenta) made during the tax year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Submit the DGI payment receipts for each quarter; non-resident-owned companies must fund the quarterly amounts from Panama accounts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax liability less advance payments and withholding credits; if positive, payment accompanies the return; if negative, a refund claim is generated.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any refund will be credited to the company's registered Panamanian bank account; non-resident shareholders cannot receive the refund.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a surcharge of 10% of the tax due, plus default interest computed at 1% per month or fraction thereof (capped at 30% under the Tax Code), and fines of up to USD 1,000 for unfiled returns or evasion. Non-filing of a zero-liability return incurs administrative fines of USD 50 to USD 500, plus suspension of the commercial license.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% for dividends paid out of profits that were subject to Panamanian corporate income tax; 15% for dividends paid out of profits not subject to tax (including foreign-source or exempt profits). A special 5% rate applies to Colon Free Zone distributions only.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a reduced dividend withholding tax under a Panama DTA, the beneficial owner must deliver a current Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) to the Panamanian paying company before the dividend is distributed. The company must retain the TRC and submit it to the DGI through the e-Tax platform as supporting documentation for the reduced-rate withholding; if the TRC is not submitted, the statutory 10%/15% rate applies. Additional documentation may include apostilled proof of beneficial ownership and a Form 300 certificate of residence for treaty purposes.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 12.5% statutory remittance tax on payments to non-residents for intellectual property licensing and know-how, unless reduced by an applicable DTA. Interest: 10% statutory withholding on interest paid to foreign creditors, except interest on loans from registered foreign financial institutions (exempt under Article 341 of the Tax Code); treaty rates may further reduce interest withholding.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: B/.250,000 (USD 250,000) - annual aggregate related-party transactions exceeding this threshold trigger mandatory Local File documentation; Master File is required when the multinational group's consolidated revenue exceeds B/.13 million (Panama TP regulation).
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama's Economic Substance Regulations (Law 70 of 2019, Executive Decree 31 of 2020) apply to companies performing defined 'relevant activities' such as distribution and service centers, IP holding, financing, leasing, shipping, and head-office services. A purely local online retailer of maternity/infant supplies is not a relevant activity unless it operates as a related-party distribution hub or derives passive income; nevertheless, the company must file the annual declaration of beneficial owners and maintain demonstrated local management and operational capacity if any cross-border related-party arrangement exists.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly omitting e-commerce revenue, inflating deductions, issuing false invoices, or using shell sales data to reduce Panama-source taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine equal to twice to five times the evaded tax, plus monthly default interest; criminal sanctions under the Penal Code (money fraud) including imprisonment of 2 to 5 years and the loss of all tax incentives; the S.A.'s commercial license may be revoked.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, the resident agent, or the financial officer who signs false returns are solidarily liable for the evaded tax and face criminal imprisonment, travel bans, asset embargoes, and seizure of personal assets; courts may pierce the corporate veil upon proof of fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the S.A. without genuine commercial activity or failing to file/report the ultimate beneficial owner(s) in Panama's Registro de Beneficiarios Finales (Law 52 of 2016), or using nominee directors/shareholders to conceal control.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to USD 10,000 per infraction, cancellation of the legal entity's rights and licenses, and immediate recording of the deficiency in the Public Registry; repeat violations may lead to a dissolution order.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors and resident agents face personal fines and may be removed from the registry; beneficial owners found to have concealed control may be subjected to AML investigation, asset attachment, travel restrictions, and, if fraud is proven, criminal prosecution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the e-commerce store as a front for laundering proceeds, accepting crypto or card payments on behalf of unauthorized third parties, or structuring transactions through Stripe/PayPal to bypass Panama's AML surveillance thresholds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money laundering offenses under Law 23 of 2015 carry penalties of 5 to 12 years' imprisonment, fines equivalent to twice the value of the laundered property, and confiscation of the financial infrastructure (bank accounts and payment processor contracts).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who knowingly facilitate the channeling of funds face criminal imprisonment, travel bans, and personal confiscation orders; the corporate veil is lifted automatically for money laundering, exposing directors' personal assets to civil and penal liability.
